title_as_printed: Experimental Values for the Vapor-Pressure (or Mole-Fraction) Enhancement Factor fw for Water in Oxygen

footnotes_as_printed.a: Each value is the mean of, on the average, five results.

pressure_note: p is the total pressure in the saturator (water vapour plus oxygen); text: 'the partial pressure pw of the vapor is the product of the vapor mole fraction xw and the total pressure', f_w = p_w/p_w^o and x_w = f_w p_w^o(T)/p, with p_w^o the saturation vapor pressure of pure water (Wexler 1976)

value.what: vapor-pressure (mole-fraction) enhancement factor of water in oxygen, f_w = p_w/p_w^o = x_w p / p_w^o (Eq 2-3); water mole fraction in the oxygen-rich gas x_w = f_w p_w^o(T)/p

composition.other_species: pure water (liquid, saturated with oxygen); no salt; gas phase is oxygen with an estimated 0.4 vol% argon impurity

conversion_needs: x_w = f_w * p_w^o(T) / p requires the saturation vapor pressure of water at T (the paper cites Wexler 1976 but does not tabulate it)
not defined: 'standard conditions' for gas volumes (no gas volumes in this paper)
notes: Restacked from the printed wide layout (columns t = 25, 50, 75 C, rows by pressure) to long form, one row per (T, p) measurement; the printed table has 5 pressure rows by 3 temperature columns with one empty cell (75 C at 2.1580 MPa, no measurement), 14 values. Each value is the mean of on average five runs, each individually adjusted to the nominal T and p. T and p are nominal values. Nominal T given in C as header 't = 25 C'.
